models.observations: The paired unequal gables survive at 40 pixels. Blue arched glazing, a clay doorstep jar and luminous ridge trim give the pearl shell a domestic scale. The left eave misses the supporting wall and a grazing view loses the greenery under the blooms. The three serialized levels validated at 416/186/114 triangles.
defects: Across all LODs the wall envelope stops below the left folded roof. At x=-0.373 the roof underside is y=0.3496 and the wall stops at y=0.336. Raise the end of the wall into the underside and seat the other roof sections continuously.

At LOD0 both leaf planes supporting the three blossoms turn away from a grazing right-side view. The flower heads then appear suspended above the sill. Add narrow solid stems from inside the planter to the base of each flower, or model foliage with volume. Verify from yaw 268 degrees.

models.observations: The folded shell now meets the wall along both slopes in the low front and reverse views. The twin roof peaks remain distinct at 40 pixels and across all three LODs. The planted sill shows green stalks below the pink heads even in the grazing right view. Gold edges, cyan ridge seams and the doorstep jar remain legible in the published preview. The exported levels validated at 425/186/114 triangles.

The grazing views show the blooms joined to the wooden box. The pearl dome, separate halo and three load-bearing gold brackets remain identifiable from the rear and across the three levels. The blue glass drum and arched front door still read at phone size. All serialized levels validated at 572/326/179.

The solar A-frame and full-height blue gable carry into the smallest phone view. A reverse view shows the shell meeting the rear glass, and the low levels retain the entrance and continuous roof outline. Green stems now reach the flowers above the window box from both side approaches. All serialized levels validated at 266/150/70.

The glazed upper bow is distinct at each LOD. The rear view shows the rooftop collector and aerial; the bright slab edges and window grouping distinguish the skydeck from the modern villa at phone size. The front planting now has a continuous green support beneath each bloom in grazing views. The levels validated at 405/235/103.

The asymmetric roof valley reads at 40 pixels and survives both lower levels. The hanging cloth behind the house, front rain chain and window box give separate details on different approaches. A lateral inspection shows the new flower stems anchored in the trough. All three levels validated at 304/142/66.

The timber upper floor is set back from a continuous roof terrace. The hanging laundry and rail distinguish the rear view; the blue glazing and stepped volumes remain legible on the two simplified levels. A grazing front-sill view shows the flowers physically joined to the box. The exported levels validated at 366/184/74.

The attic window band, paired pots and warm lower light identify the weaving house at phone size. The revised gable and rear eave return are continuous in the reverse view and the main slate silhouette persists at LOD2. The flower heads stand on visible stalks from the side; the small letter box remains beside the entry. The serialized levels validated at 508/312/126.

The opposite slope of the entry wing is now continuous slate in all three LODs. High overhead and rear views show the kitchen roof terminating against the main wing. The projecting window gable and bracketed entry still read as separate masses on a phone. Grazing views show the blossoms supported by rooted green stems. The serialized levels validated at 546/344/164.
